requirements.quote: It must be unique across all clients connecting to a single broker, and is the key in handling Message IDs messages with QoS levels 1 and 2. If the Client ID contains more than 23 characters, the broker responds to the CONNECT message with a CONNACK return code 2: Identifier Rejected.
requirements.condition: Multiple clients connect to a single broker.
requirements.required_behavior: Each connecting client must use a unique Client ID.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Two clients connecting to the same broker must not use the same Client ID.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation test can establish concurrent connections and compare the Client IDs accepted by one broker.

requirements.quote: If the Client ID contains more than 23 characters, the broker responds to the CONNECT message with a CONNACK return code 2: Identifier Rejected.
requirements.condition: A CONNECT Client ID contains more than 23 characters.
requirements.error_behavior: The broker must respond with CONNACK return code 2, Identifier Rejected.
requirements.why_checkable: A CONNECT packet with an overlength Client ID can be sent and the returned CONNACK code inspected.

requirements.quote: Will Topic The second UTF-encoded string.
requirements.condition: A CONNECT message contains the Will fields.
requirements.required_behavior: The Will Topic must be represented as the second UTF-encoded string.
requirements.why_checkable: The CONNECT payload can be decoded and the position and encoding of the Will Topic inspected.

requirements.quote: The Will Message is published to the Will Topic.
requirements.condition: The broker publishes the Will Message.
requirements.required_behavior: The broker must publish it to the Will Topic.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The broker must not publish the Will Message to a different topic.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can trigger Will publication and observe its destination topic.

requirements.quote: The QoS level is defined by the Will QoS field, and the RETAIN status is defined by the Will RETAIN flag in the variable header.
requirements.condition: A broker publishes a Will Message.
requirements.required_behavior: The publication QoS level must be determined by the CONNECT variable header's Will QoS field.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can vary the Will QoS field and inspect the QoS of the resulting Will publication.

requirements.quote: The QoS level is defined by the Will QoS field, and the RETAIN status is defined by the Will RETAIN flag in the variable header.
requirements.condition: A broker publishes a Will Message.
requirements.required_behavior: The publication RETAIN status must be determined by the CONNECT variable header's Will RETAIN flag.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can vary the Will RETAIN flag and inspect the RETAIN status of the resulting publication.

requirements.quote: Will Message The third UTF-encoded string.
requirements.condition: A CONNECT message contains the Will fields.
requirements.required_behavior: The Will Message must be represented as the third UTF-encoded string.
requirements.why_checkable: The CONNECT payload can be decoded and the position and encoding of the Will Message inspected.

requirements.quote: The Will Message defines the content of the message that is published to the Will Topic if the client is unexpectedly disconnected.
requirements.condition: A client with a configured Will Message is unexpectedly disconnected.
requirements.required_behavior: The broker must publish a message whose content is the configured Will Message to the Will Topic.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can configure a Will, force an unexpected disconnect, and compare the resulting topic and content.

requirements.quote: Although the Will Message is UTF-encoded in the CONNECT message, when it is published to the Will Topic only the bytes of the message are sent, not the first two length bytes.
requirements.condition: A Will Message from CONNECT is published to the Will Topic.
requirements.required_behavior: The broker must publish only the message bytes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The broker must not include the first two UTF length bytes in the published payload.
requirements.why_checkable: The configured encoded Will value and resulting PUBLISH payload can be compared byte for byte.

requirements.quote: The message sent when the broker executes the Will Message is raw ASCII, not UTF-encoded.
requirements.condition: The broker executes and sends a Will Message.
requirements.required_behavior: The sent Will Message must be raw ASCII.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The sent Will Message must not be UTF-encoded.
requirements.why_checkable: The emitted Will payload can be inspected for raw bytes and absence of UTF length encoding.

requirements.quote: The broker sends a CONNACK message in response to a CONNECT message from a client.
requirements.condition: The broker receives a CONNECT message from a client.
requirements.required_behavior: The broker must send a CONNACK response.
requirements.why_checkable: A client can send CONNECT and observe the broker's next protocol response.

requirements.quote: If the client does not receive a CONNACK message from the broker within a "reasonable" amount of time, the client closes the TCP/IP socket connection, and restarts the session by opening a socket to the broker and issuing a CONNECT message. A "reasonable" amount of time depends on the type of application and the communications infrastructure.
requirements.condition: No CONNACK is received within a reasonable amount of time.
requirements.required_behavior: The client closes the socket, opens a new socket to the broker, and issues a new CONNECT message.
requirements.why_checkable: The required transition is observable, but the triggering duration is application- and infrastructure-dependent and has no objective bound in this chunk.

requirements.quote: byte 1 Message type (2) DUP flag QoS flags RETAIN 0 0 1 0 x x x x
requirements.condition: A CONNACK fixed header is encoded.
requirements.required_behavior: The fixed header message-type field must have value 2.
requirements.why_checkable: The high-order message-type bits of an encoded CONNACK can be inspected.

requirements.quote: byte 2 Remaining Length (2) 0 0 0 0 0 0 1 0
requirements.condition: A CONNACK fixed header is encoded.
requirements.required_behavior: The Remaining Length must be 2.
requirements.why_checkable: The CONNACK Remaining Length byte can be decoded and compared with 2.

requirements.quote: The DUP, QoS and RETAIN flags are not used in the CONNACK message.
requirements.condition: A CONNACK message is processed.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The DUP, QoS, and RETAIN flag positions must not be assigned CONNACK semantics.
requirements.why_checkable: Static inspection or focused tests can determine whether CONNACK processing relies on these flags.

requirements.quote: Topic Name Compression Response byte 1 Reserved values. Not used. x x x x x x x x
requirements.condition: The first byte of the CONNACK variable header is processed.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The reserved byte must not be used for protocol behavior.
requirements.why_checkable: Static inspection can determine whether the implementation interprets the reserved byte, although the chunk supplies no required bit value.

requirements.quote: The values for the one byte unsigned Connect return code field are shown in the table below.
requirements.condition: A CONNACK Connect Return Code field is encoded or decoded.
requirements.required_behavior: The field must be represented as a one-byte unsigned value.
requirements.why_checkable: The variable-header field width and numeric interpretation can be inspected directly.

requirements.quote: Enumeration HEX Meaning 0 0x00 Connection Accepted
requirements.condition: The CONNACK Connect Return Code is 0x00.
requirements.required_behavior: The code must mean Connection Accepted.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's encoding, decoding, and handling of code 0x00 can be tested.

requirements.quote: 1 0x01 Connection Refused: unacceptable protocol version
requirements.condition: The CONNACK Connect Return Code is 0x01.
requirements.required_behavior: The code must mean Connection Refused due to an unacceptable protocol version.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's encoding, decoding, and handling of code 0x01 can be tested.

requirements.quote: 2 0x02 Connection Refused: identifier rejected
requirements.condition: The CONNACK Connect Return Code is 0x02.
requirements.required_behavior: The code must mean Connection Refused because the identifier was rejected.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's encoding, decoding, and handling of code 0x02 can be tested.

requirements.quote: 3 0x03 Connection Refused: broker unavailable
requirements.condition: The CONNACK Connect Return Code is 0x03.
requirements.required_behavior: The code must mean Connection Refused because the broker is unavailable.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's encoding, decoding, and handling of code 0x03 can be tested.

requirements.quote: 4-255 Reserved for future use
requirements.condition: A CONNACK Connect Return Code is selected for transmission.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Values 4 through 255 must not be used as currently defined return codes.
requirements.why_checkable: Generated CONNACK packets can be checked for use of the reserved range.

requirements.quote: Return code 2 (identifier rejected) is sent if the unique client identifier is not between 1 and 23 characters in length.
requirements.condition: A CONNECT client identifier has a length outside the inclusive range 1 through 23 characters.
requirements.error_behavior: The broker must send return code 2, identifier rejected.
requirements.why_checkable: Boundary tests with identifier lengths of 0, 1, 23, and 24 can inspect the returned code.

requirements.quote: Payload There is no payload.
requirements.condition: A CONNACK message is encoded.
requirements.required_behavior: The CONNACK payload must be empty.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A CONNACK message must not contain payload bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: The packet length and bytes following the variable header can be inspected.

requirements.quote: A message that is published to a specific topic name is delivered to connected subscribers for that topic.
requirements.condition: A message is published to a specific topic name and matching subscribers are connected.
requirements.required_behavior: The broker must deliver the message to connected subscribers for that topic.
requirements.why_checkable: A broker test can connect matching subscribers, publish to the topic, and observe delivery.

requirements.quote: To maintain symmetry, if a client subscribes to one or more topics, any message published to those topics are sent by the broker to the client as a PUBLISH message.
requirements.condition: A client subscribes to one or more topics and a message is published to one of those topics.
requirements.required_behavior: The broker must send the message to that client as a PUBLISH message.
requirements.why_checkable: A subscription and matching publication can be exercised while inspecting the outbound packet type.

requirements.quote: byte 1 Message type (3) DUP flag QoS level RETAIN 0 0 1 1 0 0 1 0
requirements.condition: A PUBLISH fixed header is encoded.
requirements.required_behavior: The fixed header message-type field must have value 3.
requirements.why_checkable: The high-order message-type bits of an encoded PUBLISH packet can be inspected.

requirements.quote: QoS level Set to 1.
requirements.condition: The PUBLISH fixed header described in this passage is encoded.
requirements.required_behavior: The QoS level must be set to 1.
requirements.why_checkable: The QoS bits in the described PUBLISH fixed header can be decoded and compared with 1.

requirements.quote: DUP flag Set to zero (0). This means that the message is being sent for the first time.
requirements.condition: A PUBLISH message is sent for the first time.
requirements.required_behavior: The DUP flag must be set to 0.
requirements.why_checkable: The first transmission of a PUBLISH packet can be captured and its DUP bit inspected.

requirements.quote: For messages with QoS level 1 or level 2 that are being re-sent because a failure has been detected, the DUP bit is set to 1.
requirements.condition: A QoS 1 or QoS 2 PUBLISH message is retransmitted because a failure was detected.
requirements.required_behavior: The DUP bit must be set to 1.
requirements.why_checkable: A failure and retransmission can be induced and the retransmitted fixed header inspected.

requirements.quote: This indicates to the broker that the message might duplicate a message that has already been received.
requirements.condition: A broker receives a PUBLISH message with DUP set to 1.
requirements.required_behavior: The broker must interpret the flag as indicating that the message might duplicate one already received.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The broker must not treat DUP=1 as proof that the message is necessarily new.
requirements.why_checkable: Broker duplicate-handling logic can be inspected or exercised with repeated message identifiers.

requirements.quote: The DUP bit is not used for messages with QoS level 0.
requirements.condition: A PUBLISH message has QoS level 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The DUP bit must not affect processing of the message.
requirements.why_checkable: QoS 0 messages with differing DUP values can be compared for equivalent processing.

requirements.quote: RETAIN flag Set to zero. This means do not retain.
requirements.condition: The PUBLISH fixed header described in this passage is encoded.
requirements.required_behavior: The RETAIN flag must be set to 0 and the message must not be retained.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The broker must not retain the message represented by this flag value.
requirements.why_checkable: The header bit and subsequent retained-message behavior can both be tested.

requirements.quote: Remaining Length field The length of the variable header plus the length of the payload.
requirements.condition: A PUBLISH Remaining Length field is encoded.
requirements.required_behavior: Its value must equal the variable-header length plus the payload length.
requirements.why_checkable: The field can be decoded and compared with the measured lengths of both packet sections.

requirements.quote: It can be a multibyte field.
requirements.condition: A PUBLISH Remaining Length value requires more than one byte.
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation must support a multibyte Remaining Length field.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The implementation must not assume the field is always one byte.
requirements.why_checkable: Packets whose Remaining Length uses multiple bytes can be encoded or decoded in a focused test.

requirements.quote: Variable header The variable header contains the following fields: Topic name A UTF-encoded string.
requirements.condition: A PUBLISH variable header is encoded.
requirements.required_behavior: It must contain a UTF-encoded Topic name.
requirements.why_checkable: The variable header can be parsed for presence and encoding of the Topic name.

requirements.quote: Message ID Present for messages with QoS level 1 and QoS level 2.
requirements.condition: A PUBLISH message has QoS level 1 or QoS level 2.
requirements.required_behavior: A Message ID must be present in the variable header.
requirements.why_checkable: QoS 1 and QoS 2 PUBLISH variable headers can be parsed for the field.

requirements.quote: A Message ID must not be used in the variable header for messages with QoS level 0.
requirements.condition: A PUBLISH message has QoS level 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A Message ID must not appear in the variable header.
requirements.why_checkable: A QoS 0 PUBLISH packet can be parsed to confirm the field is absent.

requirements.quote: The Message ID is a 16-bit unsigned integer, which typically increases by exactly one from one message to the next, but is not required to do so.
requirements.condition: A PUBLISH Message ID is encoded or decoded.
requirements.required_behavior: The Message ID must be represented as a 16-bit unsigned integer.
requirements.why_checkable: The field width and unsigned interpretation can be inspected directly.

requirements.quote: The Message ID is a 16-bit unsigned integer, which typically increases by exactly one from one message to the next, but is not required to do so.
requirements.condition: Successive valid PUBLISH Message IDs are processed.
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation must permit Message IDs that do not increase by exactly one.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The implementation must not require exact sequential increments between Message IDs.
requirements.why_checkable: Nonsequential, nonzero 16-bit Message IDs can be supplied and acceptance observed.

requirements.quote: The ordering of the 2 bytes of the Message Identifier is MSB, then LSB (big-endian).
requirements.condition: A PUBLISH Message Identifier is serialized or parsed.
requirements.required_behavior: The most significant byte must precede the least significant byte.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The identifier must not be serialized in little-endian order.
requirements.why_checkable: The two wire bytes can be inspected using a Message Identifier with unequal bytes.

requirements.quote: Message ID 0 (that is, 0x0000) is reserved as an invalid Message ID, and must not be used.
requirements.condition: A PUBLISH Message ID is selected or encoded.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Message ID 0x0000 must not be used.
requirements.why_checkable: Generated PUBLISH packets and identifier-allocation logic can be checked for zero.

requirements.quote: Payload Contains the data for publishing.
requirements.condition: A PUBLISH message carries application data.
requirements.required_behavior: The publishing data must be placed in the PUBLISH payload.
requirements.why_checkable: The serialized packet can be parsed and its payload compared with the supplied publishing data.

requirements.quote: The Remaining Length field in the fixed header includes both the variable header length and the payload length.
requirements.condition: A PUBLISH fixed header is encoded.
requirements.required_behavior: The Remaining Length must include both the variable-header length and the payload length.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Neither the variable header nor payload may be omitted from the Remaining Length calculation.
requirements.why_checkable: The declared value can be compared against both measured sections of the packet.

requirements.quote: QoS Level Expected response QoS 0 None QoS 1 PUBACK QoS 2 PUBREC
requirements.condition: A QoS 0 PUBLISH message is received.
requirements.required_behavior: No protocol response is expected.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A PUBACK or PUBREC response must not be required for QoS 0.
requirements.why_checkable: A QoS 0 PUBLISH exchange can be observed for absence of an acknowledgment response.

requirements.quote: QoS Level Expected response QoS 0 None QoS 1 PUBACK QoS 2 PUBREC
requirements.condition: A QoS 1 PUBLISH message is received.
requirements.required_behavior: The expected response is PUBACK.
requirements.why_checkable: A QoS 1 PUBLISH exchange can be observed and the response packet type inspected.

requirements.quote: QoS Level Expected response QoS 0 None QoS 1 PUBACK QoS 2 PUBREC
requirements.condition: A QoS 2 PUBLISH message is received.
requirements.required_behavior: The expected response is PUBREC.
requirements.why_checkable: A QoS 2 PUBLISH exchange can be observed and the response packet type inspected.

requirements.quote: PUBLISH messages can be sent either from a publisher to the broker, or from the broker to a subscriber.
requirements.condition: A PUBLISH message is transmitted.
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation must support PUBLISH transmission from publisher to broker and from broker to subscriber.
requirements.why_checkable: Both permitted directions can be exercised in integration tests.

requirements.quote: The action of the recipient when it receives a message depends on the QoS level of the message: QoS 0 Make the message available to any interested parties.
requirements.condition: A recipient receives a QoS 0 PUBLISH message.
requirements.required_behavior: The recipient must make the message available to interested parties.
requirements.why_checkable: A QoS 0 publication can be delivered while observing whether registered interested parties receive it.
